## What it does

<!-- BEGIN AUTO-GENERATED: overview -->
Workshop guidance for using Microsoft AI Discovery Cards to ideate AI agents after problem framing.
<!-- END AUTO-GENERATED: overview -->

## When to use it

Use this skill during Method 4 brainstorming when a team wants AI-focused
inspiration after validating its problem statement, persona, user needs, and
How Might We questions. The DT Coach and DT Learning Tutor load it on demand;
it is not a standalone slash command.

Use the [Microsoft AI Discovery Cards Workshop Facilitation Guide](https://aka.ms/aidiscoverycards)
as the authoritative source for card content and workshop details. Connect ideas
to a validated user journey and capture assumptions and human decision points
without treating the cards as proof of feasibility or a required architecture.

If the problem or stakeholder need is unclear, return to the Problem Space
methods before introducing the cards. Keep evaluation separate from divergent
ideation, then assess selected directions during convergence and concept development.

## Example usage

After completing Method 3, ask the DT Coach:

```text
Our research shows that maintenance planners struggle to find relevant repair
history before scheduling work. Our How Might We question is: How might we help
planners use repair history when preparing maintenance tasks?
Use AI Discovery Cards to broaden our Method 4 brainstorming.
```

The coach loads this skill and directs the facilitator to the official guide.
Participants apply the cards to the planner's journey, defer judgment while
generating ideas, and add those ideas to the Method 4 inventory. Each idea records
the user need it addresses, relevant constraints, and unverified assumptions.
For agentic ideas, participants also identify where a human retains a decision.

Selected themes move into Method 5 concepts and Method 6 prototypes before
entering RPI research. The workshop does not establish that a proposed AI
capability is available, safe, or technically feasible.
